body.statement: For every \(z>0\), the limiting coverage of the conventional selected interval is \(C_z(k)\). At an exact selector tie, \(C_z(0)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for all \(\rho_1,\rho_2\in[-1,1]\). For any fixed \(z>0\), \(C_z(k)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) if and only if \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\). If \(k\neq0\) and \(\rho_1^2\neq\rho_2^2\), then \(\operatorname{sign}\{C_z(k)-[2\Phi(z)-1]\}=\operatorname{sign}\{k(\rho_1^2-\rho_2^2)\}\).
body.justification: The coverage function separates harmless selected asymmetry from genuine two-sided Wald distortion and gives its strict direction.
body.gap: Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald give comparator-specific Gaussian coverage formulas, and Azzalini--Regoli give even-functional symmetry; neither gives this selected-coordinate all-gap if-and-only-if boundary.
body.consumer: The equality \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\) is a feasible robustness diagnostic for deciding whether conventional role-selected intervals require correction.
body.proof_tex:
Each \(T_s=(A_s+\sqrt rR_s)/\sqrt{V_s}\) is marginally standard normal.  The independent centered Gaussian post coordinate is included in this covariance statement, and \(\rho_s=\operatorname{Corr}(T_s,X)\).  In particular, \(\Pr(T_s=\pm z)=0\).  The boundary of the selected event \(\{|T_{J(d)}|\leq z\}\) is contained in \(\{T_1=\pm z\}\cup\{T_2=\pm z\}\cup\{X=k\}\), which has probability zero by the marginal variance assumptions.  Continuous upper and lower approximations to its indicator therefore show from \(\texttt{thm:selected-gaussian-limit}\) that the finite-sample Wald coverage converges to the probability calculated below.  For \(|\rho_s|<1\), completing the square in the joint Gaussian density gives
\[
 T_s\mid X=x\sim N(\rho_sx,1-\rho_s^2),
\]
so
\[
 \Pr\{|T_s|\leq z\mid X=x\}
 =\Phi\!\left(\frac{z-\rho_sx}{\sqrt{1-\rho_s^2}}\right)
  -\Phi\!\left(\frac{-z-\rho_sx}{\sqrt{1-\rho_s^2}}\right)
 =g_{\rho_s}(x;z).
\]
The selected limit in \(\texttt{thm:selected-gaussian-limit}\) chooses role one on \(\{X\leq k\}\) and role two on its complement.  Conditioning on \(X\), whose density is \(\phi\), therefore proves
\[
 \Pr\{|T_1|\leq z,X\leq k\}
 +\Pr\{|T_2|\leq z,X>k\}
 =\int_{-\infty}^{k}\phi(x)g_{\rho_1}(x;z)\,dx
  +\int_k^{\infty}\phi(x)g_{\rho_2}(x;z)\,dx
 =C_z(k).
\]
The formulas for \(|\rho_s|=1\) follow by weak convergence as \(|\rho_s|\uparrow1\), equivalently by using the degenerate conditional law \(T_s=\rho_sX\).

For every \(\rho\in[-1,1]\), symmetry of the interval gives
\[
 g_\rho(-x;z)=g_\rho(x;z),
 \qquad
 \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\phi(x)g_\rho(x;z)\,dx
 =\Pr\{|T|\leq z\}=2\Phi(z)-1.
\]
Thus each half-line through zero contains one half of the unselected symmetric coverage, and
\[
 C_z(0)=\frac12\{2\Phi(z)-1\}
       +\frac12\{2\Phi(z)-1\}=2\Phi(z)-1.
\]

It remains to prove both necessity and the strict sign.  For \(a>0\) and \(q\in[0,1]\), let
\[
 R_z(a,q)=\Pr_q\{|X|\leq a,\ |T|\leq z\},
\]
where \((X,T)\) is bivariate standard normal with nonnegative correlation \(q\).  Because symmetric rectangles are unchanged by replacing \(T\) with \(-T\), \(R_z(a,q)\) depends on a correlation only through its absolute value.  For \(0<q<1\), let \(f_q\) denote the bivariate standard-normal density.  Direct differentiation of its displayed exponential formula gives
\[
 \frac{\partial f_q(x,t)}{\partial q}
 =\frac{\partial^2f_q(x,t)}{\partial x\,\partial t}.
\]
Integrating this identity over \([-a,a]\times[-z,z]\) and evaluating the four corners yields
\[
 \frac{\partial R_z(a,q)}{\partial q}
 =2\{f_q(a,z)-f_q(a,-z)\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{f_q(a,z)}{f_q(a,-z)}
 =\exp\!\left(\frac{2qaz}{1-q^2}\right)>1
 \qquad(a,z,q>0).
\]
Hence \(R_z(a,q)\) is strictly increasing in \(q\) on \([0,1]\), with strictness at zero and continuity at one obtained by integrating the positive derivative over every nonempty subinterval and then taking limits.

Using the evenness already proved, for every \(k\ne0\),
\[
 C_z(k)-\{2\Phi(z)-1\}
 =\frac{\operatorname{sign}(k)}{2}
 \left[R_z(|k|,|\rho_1|)-R_z(|k|,|\rho_2|)\right].
\]
Strict monotonicity gives
\[
 \operatorname{sign}\!\left(C_z(k)-[2\Phi(z)-1]\right)
 =\operatorname{sign}\!\left(k(\rho_1^2-\rho_2^2)\right).
\]
If \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\), then \(g_{\rho_1}=g_{\rho_2}\) because conditional symmetric coverage depends only on the absolute correlation, and consequently \(C_z(k)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for every \(k\).  Conversely, if coverage is nominal for every \(k\), the strict sign formula rules out unequal squared correlations.  This proves the asserted if-and-only-if frontier and all endpoint cases.
